## Design

### 2026-10-22 – Yesterday I started designing my pcb but forgot to make a journal. But tbh yesterday and today I was doing the same thing, so yeah. I think that the pcb is almost done, tomorrow I might start coding,

**5.97h**

Yesterday I started designing my pcb but forgot to make a journal. But tbh yesterday and today I was doing the same thing, so yeah. I think that the pcb is almost done, tomorrow I might start coding, check again if everything is wired correctly, maybe add some art +  info about me and my number/email. I tried doing that today, but because this project uses like 30 resistors (not the ones that are normally used on PCBs but the ones that you can use for example on a breadboard) I just didn't had a lot of space left for what I've initially designed (also I added 30 mins because I deleted some footage where my number was visible). I'm using so many resistors because I'm going to check which key is currently touched with the stylus by checking the voltage on the analog pins. Basically a voltage divider

Overall it's going great tbh, kinda had a hard start this week because recently there were some sad and really bad things happening in my class, but I don't want to talk about this because I think it's inappropriate in this space. But hey, at least I can always go do this crap I love to do and don't think about anything else

### 2026-10-23 – I finalized the PCB today but forgot to turn on lapse. I think I spent about 1.5h working today or a little bit more, I'm really happy with how it turned out!

**1.25h**

I finalized the PCB today but forgot to turn on lapse. I think I spent about 1.5h working today or a little bit more, I'm really happy with how it turned out!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/vhPuIXXulHs6LeuYMclarNIsOTRiD2p5/8eaeb4450aaa9f961bd0b84876699ebca18388e3520f5eefbfb96d29f235d1fa.png)

The arduino pro micro I'm using is a clone, it  has a USB C port and is a bit longer, so I'll be flush with the PCB compared to the one on the renders. Also it's going to sit on the back, so the buzzer won't collide with it.

I'm going to detect which key is currently "pressed" by checking the voltage on the analog pins connected to some voltage dividers - that's why there are so many resistors. Basically a cable with a crocodile clip is clipped to that lightning (that's connected to gnd) and touching different pads with the other end changes the resistance - and so the voltage on the analog pins - Ohm's law. Also I'll be able to change the range octave up or add a little bit of vibrato to the sound by pressing the buttons on the side.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/vhPuIXXulHs6LeuYMclarNIsOTRiD2p5/500c5e2c742b110b7cebad66423cf7b83997fef67aec2cdeaef104716cb1418a.png)
On the back is my name and my phone number (but I blurred the number). Also I added a domain name I want to buy in the future.

Overall I think the PCB is done and I'll start working on the code tomorrow. Shouldn't be too hard I think!
